Q: HTML span elements inside <p> not passing automated tests for nutrition label project A:

Your HTML is visually correct, but the automated test is failing because it checks the exact textContent and node order, not how it looks in the browser.

Line breaks and indentation inside the <p> create extra whitespace text nodes, which causes the test to fail.

The <p> must contain the text exactly:

Total Fat 8g 10%

with:

  • one <span class="bold"> around Total Fat

  • plain text 8g

  • one <span class="bold"> around 10%

Put everything on one line with explicit spaces:

<p><span class="bold">Total Fat</span> 8g <span class="bold">10%</span></p>

This removes extra whitespace nodes and matches what the automated test expects.

Q: X Error of failed request: BadAlloc (insufficient resources for operation) while running tkinter A:

In a CodeReview of my code the error you mention happened to a reviewer.
The code in doubt that produced the issue was:

x = 0
for i in range(1,40_000):
    draw.line((x,0,x,400), fill=CCTInterface.temp_to_rgb(i),width=1)
    x += 1

I refactored the code as I'd advised it to you (and weren't able to provide an example 3y ago) with a generator and the error disappeared:

        def generate_gradient(range_, quality=1):
            height = 400
            background = (0,0,0,1)
            image = Image.new('RGB', (int(range_/quality),height), background)
            draw = ImageDraw.Draw(image)
            
            def generate(x):
                '''Generate gradient with lazy evaluation
                in response to this review:
                https://codereview.stackexchange.com/a/301044/228833
                '''
                for _ in range(0, range_, quality):
                    x = yield x
                    fill = CCTInterface.temp_to_rgb(x*quality)
                    draw.line((x,0,x,height),fill=fill,width=1)
                    y = x+1
                    yield y
            x = 0
            generator = generate(x)
            for _ in generator:
                try:
                    x = generator.send(x)
                except StopIteration:
                    break
            return image

The reason for the error (I assume) is that the whole sequence of a *for-loop* gets stored in memory, while generators in python working with lazy evaluation.

If a tcl-programmer stumbles upon this answer you will likely have to use the coroutine command or another part of the NRE (Non-Recursive-Engine).

Q: Are the lock and unlock methods of a mutex object considered as modifications to the object? A:

Both unlock and lock calls are obvious modifications to the mutex object which internally controls bool state of the mutex. For architecture design purposes where mutex will be used to avoid race conditions in some other object (guarded by this mutex) it is not needed to follow modifications of the mutex but its current state, or more precisely ensure that single operation in thread that involves access a shared resource (object) is started with the call to lock and ended with the call to unlock of guarding mutex object.

What makes sequence in question invalid is the fact that it is not allowed to unlock the mutex if it wasn't first locked in the same thread. Attempt to make such a call in standard library results in undefined behavior, which makes it vital to ensure proper implementation. Therefore after unlock call (from thread that locked mutex before) there will be always a call to lock that follows - either from the other or the same thread, depending on how developed system is designed and policy of operating system thread scheduler. Mutex internal architecture ensures there will be always lock/unlock calls executed properly (in pairs) assuming that the user code is implemented correctly.

In the code snippets call to lock and unlock will be executed from the same thread exactly in the order there are inserted in the source code. Order of instructions within code block always defines order of execution.
